A0255.title: Cross-Market Order Book Consistency Monitoring
A0255.definition: Compare order books, trades, spreads, and liquidity changes for the same or related instruments across venues to detect cross-venue manipulation and abnormal liquidity shifts.
A0255.description:
Cross-market order-book consistency monitoring collects depth, execution prices, spreads, cancellations, funding rates, and liquidity-shift signals across venues, instruments, and derivatives. Cross-venue baselines, lead-lag relationships, spread divergence, and common-control behavior identify paths where one venue creates false depth while another executes trades or induces breakouts.

This control detects cross-venue liquidity shifts, false-break inducement, ghost liquidity, and cross-platform market manipulation. Deployment requires lawful data access and adjustment for matching rules, market-data latency, and session differences.
A0255.limitation: Cross-market data latency, rule differences, currency and contract definitions create natural divergence; OTC and dark-pool opacity can cause false negatives. Attackers may exploit data gaps or latency windows, requiring counterparty, custody, and clearing cross-checks.
